name: GET /api/ai-gateway/health — sdk-ai-gateway
description: Liveness probe for sdk-ai-gateway. Returns 200 with the constant body { sdk: 'sdk-ai-gateway', status: 'ok' }. QA edge cases: this path is on the api-gateway public allowlist (isHealth matches any path ending in /health), so it is reachable with NO Authorization header and must NOT return 401 — a 401 here means the authGate allowlist regressed, which is the one regression worth asserting; the handler has no requireAuth preHandler, touches no database, provider or credential store, and takes no parameters, so it reports only that the route is mounted and cannot detect a degraded provider or an unreachable Postgres — 'ok' is not a dependency health signal; it therefore has no error responses of its own.

errorCases.when: sdk-ai-gateway is not mounted — its registerRoutes is only reached if the package is a workspace:* dep of services/api-gateway AND app.register(...) names it in app.ts. Forgetting either still builds cleanly, so the probe 404s from Fastify's default not-found handler instead of answering. This is the ONE failure this endpoint exists to catch, and the reason it is worth an assertion at all.
any method other than GET/HEAD — the route is registered with app.get, and Fastify matches on method+path, so a wrong verb is a route miss rather than a 405

_noHandlerErrorsNote: The handler itself has NO error branch: it is `async () => ({ sdk: 'sdk-ai-gateway', status: 'ok' })` — no body parsing, no params, no database, no provider or credential read, no throw. Every error a caller can observe on this path therefore comes from routing, which is what the two cases above document. In particular there is no 401: isHealth() in the gateway authGate matches any path ending in /health, so the probe answers identically with no Authorization header, an expired token or a garbage one — a 401 here means the allowlist regressed.
